_comment: Regression seeds: failure patterns the eval has caught and that must not silently re-enter the codebase. Each entry references a case_id that already lives in golden.json (so the case is exercised by the standard eval run). run_evals.load_cases() reads this file at runtime and emits a warning if any seeded case_id has been removed from golden.json — that's the drift guard. To add a new regression seed: add the entry here AND ensure the corresponding case is present in golden.json with full annotation.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Option B — multi_part_complaint rule for draft-response
seeds.description: Multi-part complaint where the responder honestly hedges some sub-issues but makes an assertive fix-like claim about another sub-issue at low overall confidence (< 0.4). The judge ruled this misleading_fix_claim. The multi_part_complaint rule added to draft-response targets exactly this pattern.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Option B — multi_part_complaint rule for draft-response
seeds.description: Same multi-part pattern as civ7_gameplay_002. The judge's ruling on this case has been borderline across recent runs (sometimes honest_hedge, sometimes misleading_fix_claim). Locked here so future regressions on the same pattern are caught.
seeds.judge_ruling_before_fix: borderline (honest_hedge or misleading_fix_claim depending on prompt revision)

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iteration 1 — action_severity_precedence rules for draft-response + critique-draft
seeds.description: Two-rung downward action swap (escalate → monitor) on a review explicitly using hard-blocker language ('unplayable', 'crashing constantly', 'pervasive'). Pre-fix the responder defaulted DOWN the action ladder under low patch confidence. Rule 1 (severity-overrides-confidence) targets exactly this — hard-blocker language must produce escalate regardless of patch evidence confidence.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iteration 1 — action_severity_precedence rules for draft-response + critique-draft
seeds.description: One-rung upward action swap (no_action → monitor) on a pure DLC-pricing opinion ('half the game locked behind dlcs'). Pre-fix the responder treated subjective monetization feedback as trackable. Rule 2 (subjectivity-caps-the-ladder) targets exactly this — pure pricing/design opinion defaults to no_action and the existence of related patches does not raise the rung.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iteration 1 — action_severity_precedence rules for draft-response + critique-draft
seeds.description: Negative-direction guard for Rule 1. This case mentions hard-blocker language ('pretty much unplayable') but its ideal action is monitor, not escalate — the complaint is a multiplayer-server lag pattern, not a hard-blocker crash. Locked to catch future drift where Rule 1 over-fires on the bare presence of hard-blocker words. The case must STAY at proposed_action == 'monitor'; promotion to escalate is the regression this seed guards.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iter5 — critique-draft header-block consultation (monitor-on-design over-rejection fix)
seeds.description: Win-side seed for the Iter5 critic header-block surgery. Pre-fix, this case (a recurring design complaint about Act One pacing in PoE2) was repeatedly rejected at iter0 with critic critique 'monitor is incorrect... should be escalated to investigate'. The line-59 guardrail ('adjacent-rung disagreements monitor↔investigate are tolerable') was buried at the bottom of check #6 and being silently overridden. After moving the rung definitions to <action_rubric_reference> and promoting the guardrail to the lead of check #6, the critic should treat this as a tolerable adjacent-rung call and approve at monitor. Drift guard: any future edit that re-buries the guardrail or removes the adjacent-rung tolerance will surface as this case landing on investigate.
seeds.judge_ruling_before_fix: n/a (final draft was action-correct, but iter0 was rejected and the case burned iterations)
seeds.expected_outcome_after_fix: action_correctness.correct == True (proposed_action == 'monitor') AND ideally iter0_approval == True

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iter5 — critique-draft header-block consultation (monitor-on-design over-rejection fix)
seeds.description: Second win-side seed for the Iter5 critic surgery. Pre-fix, the responder's monitor proposal on this systemic design complaint (build diversity / boss design feedback) was rejected at iter0 with critic critique 'monitor is inappropriate... it belongs in no_action' — a no_action↔monitor adjacent rejection that the line-59 guardrail should also tolerate when the critic's confidence is low. After the cognitive-ordering inversion in check #6, this case should converge cleanly to monitor without the iter0 thrash. Locked alongside poe2_content_001 to give the regression suite two examples of the same pattern across different ladder neighborhoods (monitor↔investigate AND no_action↔monitor).
seeds.judge_ruling_before_fix: n/a (final draft was action-correct after iteration, but iter0 was rejected)

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iter5 — critique-draft header-block consultation (pricing-as-no_action negative control)
seeds.description: Negative-direction guard for the Iter5 critic surgery. The header-block restructuring of check #6 must NOT relax fail condition #2 (over-escalation upward), which is what keeps pure pricing/monetization complaints at no_action even when they describe related game features. This case is a Starfield monetization complaint with ideal_action=no_action — after the edit, **it should still land at no_action; any acceptance of investigate or escalate is a failure of fail-condition #2.** The plan dropped README's candidate fix (b) (fold heated-adjective into responder) precisely to avoid weakening fail #2; this seed catches any silent drift in the same direction. Distinct from payday3_monetize_001 (Iter1 seed), which guards a different pricing review.
